next.name: GOLD RAINFOREST
next.headline: GOLD RAINFOREST: the Lapsus$ name and a 2025 alliance that borrowed it
next.in_short: Secureworks tracks GOLD RAINFOREST, also called Lapsus$. In 2025 a Telegram-based collective blended the Lapsus$, Scattered Spider and ShinyHunters names. Vendors differ on how tightly the three are linked.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks GOLD RAINFOREST. The catalogue lists its other names as Lapsus$, Slippy Spider and Strawberry Tempest.
Trustwave SpiderLabs tracks a brand called Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters. It says the brand appeared on Telegram in early August 2025 and uses assets tied to Scattered Spider, ShinyHunters and LAPSUS$.

Trustwave does not assess the brand as a formal, centralized group made up only of those three. It infers from writing style, emoji use and posting rhythm that fewer than five people drive the core operation.
Resecurity calls the three groups overlapping, social-engineering-based extortion crews. It says the overlaps suggest coordination but do not prove it.
Resecurity says the groups jointly targeted organizations in financial services, technology, retail and airlines.
Picus Labs describes victims among major brands in retail, fashion, aviation and insurance.
Trustwave says the collective focuses on cloud data theft from SaaS providers and corporate CRM systems.
The catalogue lists Mimikatz as a tool tied to GOLD RAINFOREST.
Picus Labs says LAPSUS$ used the RedLine password stealer to harvest passwords and session tokens from compromised systems.
Resecurity says both LAPSUS$ and Scattered Spider are known for help desk impersonation and credential theft.
Picus Labs describes phone-based vishing as the opening move in recent Salesforce intrusions. It also describes theft of OAuth tokens tied to customer integrations.
Trustwave says the collective publicly announced an extortion-as-a-service model.
Picus Labs dates a Telegram channel claiming to unite the three groups to 8 August 2025. Trustwave notes the channels were removed and recreated at least 16 times.
Picus Labs reports that on 12 September 2025 the FBI issued a FLASH alert. It linked a string of Salesforce breaches to two groups, UNC6040 and UNC6395.
Picus Labs says the group announced on 17 September 2025 that it was going dark. Resecurity does not believe that announcement is sincere.
One report says the attackers claim to have stolen over 1.5 billion records from 760 companies. The report presents this as a claim.
Trustwave says the collective claims to have acquired an exploit for CVE-2025-61882 in Oracle E-Business Suite. It calls the nature of that acquisition unverified.
Verify any help desk call or unexpected MFA prompt through a separate channel. Review which third-party apps are allowed to connect to your SaaS and CRM accounts.
